scope: Proposition A.6 (Far energy reduction) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 124. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume that each equation has the splitting (A.16), and that its correction, raw, remainder, and mixed budgets satisfy, in the triangular order specified below, bounds of the form oR0→∞(1)(F + Sa) + C ∑ prior Fprior + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c1 ) (A.19) for fixed c1 > 0. Assume also that the corrections have initial weighted energy and averaged starting- annulus costs bounded by the initial and overlap terms in (A.19); the annular norm is the compact weighted L2 norm. Then the two energy multipliers give F ≤ o(1)(F + Sa) + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c2 ) (A.20) (with c2 > 0, allowing analogous small input bootstrap errors). It suffices also to take tunably small uniform coefficients on F in this argument. A convenient prior order for linear terms is: level P before the h hierarchies, within a level lower total orders first, more lab times first at fixed total order, and then fewer S’s first. Small radius gains and perturbative nonlinear effects may cross this order. Norms aggregated at equal indices are treated together.
